_what: Player B selection, recorded before any of Player B's games were fetched.
selection_rule: 1. Candidate pool: every username appearing in a 180+0 or 300+0 Termination-Normal game with Elo 1580-1720 in the first 80 MB of the public lichess_db_standard_rated_2026-06 dump.
2. Excluded: erez281; every account appearing on either side of his frozen 2,209-game window; every side of the 600-game population corpus; the account used for the plumbing demo.

4. Screened in that order against the public profile: account open, blitz rating in [1626,1674] (the window whose DERIVED band is the one the registry holds), blitz games >= 400, rating not provisional. Stopped at 6 hits.

5. Chosen: the hit whose current blitz rating is closest to the band centre 1650. This preference is the task's own ('prefer a median around 1650'), stated before any screening ran; it is recorded here so the choice is mechanical rather than a matter of taste.
honesty_note: The screen in step 4 was executed before step 5 was written into this file. Step 5's criterion is not post-hoc: it is the selection preference the task stated in advance. Every screened hit is listed below so the rule can be checked against the data it was applied to.
chosen_reason: current blitz rating 1655 is the closest of the screened hits to the band centre 1650
derived_band_expected: 1450-1850, provided the fetched corpus's blitz median stays in 1626-1674; the authoritative band is derived by the pipeline from the corpus itself

window_declared_before_fetch.meaning: the 800 most recent ADMISSIBLE games, in the platform's own newest-first order (contract.WINDOW_RULE with an explicit cap)
window_declared_before_fetch.why_a_cap: livio68 has 13,539 blitz games; scoring all of them under the frozen engine regime is days of compute. The cap is declared here, before a single game of theirs was fetched, because a window chosen after seeing a corpus is a window chosen for its reading. 800 admissible games give DERIVE/VALIDATE/TEST frames well above every frozen minimum in contract.MIN_CORPUS.
window_declared_before_fetch.input_mode_consequence: this run replicates the METHODOLOGY; it does not exercise the username-only ingestion contract, because lichess answers 404 to the by-username export without a token in this environment

revision_v2.what_happened: v1 screened on the account's CURRENT blitz rating as a proxy for the median the band rule reads. Applied to the first choice, `livio68` (rated 1655 today), the median over the 269 admissible blitz games in the enumerable window came out at 1772: they slid from about 1770 to about 1660 across that window. Derived band 1550-1950, which the registry does not hold.
revision_v2.status_of_livio68: REJECTED AT ELIGIBILITY, before any position was scored. Nothing about their chess was read and no analytic choice was taken from them, so this is not a retired replication -- it is a candidate that failed a pre-analysis screen. Their frozen corpus and draft pre-registration were deleted rather than kept as if they were a run.
revision_v2.what_changed: The proxy is gone. The screen now applies the exact criterion the pipeline applies: enumerate the window, fetch it, run the frozen eligibility, take the median own_rating over admissible blitz games, and require population_band(median) to be a band the registry holds. The cheap profile-rating filter survives only as a locator, widened to 1550-1800, and decides nothing.
revision_v2.what_did_not_change: The candidate pool, the exclusion lists, the deterministic order, and the rule that the FIRST candidate to pass is taken. No research rule was touched: eligibility, splits, vocabulary, search, population correction, thresholds and output classes are exactly as frozen.
revision_v2.closeness_preference_dropped: v1 chose the hit closest to 1650 in order to land inside the registered band. Testing the band directly makes that preference redundant, and a preference that no longer does any work is one more place for taste to enter, so it is gone.
